Split the row; the compound claim is wrong as written.

`disableSideloadFlags` — **not a gap; refuted on consequence.** The key rejects `--plugin-dir`, `--plugin-url`, `--agents`, `--mcp-config` at startup to close a `strictKnownMarketplaces` bypass. Our product accepts none of those flags (positive control: the full long-flag set our CLI parses is enumerated at `apps/cli/src/index.ts:80-138`, and none of the four is in it), and there is no renamed sideload equivalent (`packages/shared/src/marketplace/install-source.ts`, `types.ts` have no local-path install source). Nothing to reject. Product-shape difference — desktop app, not the Claude CLI.

`blockedMarketplaces` — **absent, but narrower than claimed, and already recorded.** No source reader exists (`grep -ran` over `packages`/`apps` hits only vendored upstream bundles and docs), and it is absent from `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` (`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:501-534`). The real residue is polarity only: an admin can pin an allowlist but cannot block one named source while leaving others open. Recorded as a deviation with its reason at `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-marketplace-entry-authority.md:232` and `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:184` ("the allowlist is the stronger control … the blocklist adds reach not safety").
